summary: Backend-only iteration 19 verification completed against the public preview URL. The restarted deployment now passes all three email-history compatibility assertions: new recipient/error_msg rows map to to/error, legacy to/error rows remain compatible, and mixed rows prefer the new fields. Billing portal valid-origin creation also passes, but the requested open-redirect fix is not deployed: https://evil.com is accepted with HTTP 200 instead of rejected with HTTP 400. All 41 requested billing/iteration 14-16 non-provider regressions passed; email-quota-dependent delivery tests were intentionally not run.

critical.issue: Foreign origin_url https://evil.com is accepted and returns a Stripe portal_url with HTTP 200. The endpoint must reject a host different from ALERT_APP_URL with HTTP 400.

action_items: In billing_portal, pass the request/default origin through _validate_origin_url before constructing Stripe return_url, restart the backend, and rerun the iteration 19 targeted test.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/billing.py:292-297 reads origin_url directly and interpolates origin.rstrip('/') into Stripe return_url; unlike billing_checkout, it never calls _validate_origin_url. This source/deployment mismatch is the direct cause of the reproduced open redirect.

Stripe SDK network calls remain synchronous inside async FastAPI endpoints, so provider latency can block the event loop; move blocking Stripe calls to a threadpool or use an async integration in a future refactor.

success_rate.backend: 98% (45/46 executed tests passed: targeted 4/5; requested regressions 41/41)

seed_data_creation: Created temporary journal entries, new/legacy/mixed certificate-email rows, billing/regression users, Stripe test customers, Checkout Sessions, Portal Sessions, invite/auth/logo/seal resources, and expired-trial accounts. Mongo resources and Stripe test customers were cleaned up; immutable Stripe sandbox session history remains.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Rerun test_iteration18.py after applying portal origin validation. Email-history is confirmed green for all three required schemas after the backend restart. Valid portal origin returns a billing.stripe.com URL. The only targeted failure is evil.com receiving HTTP 200. Regression totals: billing 15/15, selected iteration 14 baseline 16/16, iteration 15 4/4, and iteration 16 non-provider 6/6. The provider-dependent preview/cron/real-send tests were intentionally skipped per request.
rca_of_the_issue: billing_checkout calls _validate_origin_url, but billing_portal does not. It reads body.origin_url (or ALERT_APP_URL) and directly builds return_url, so an authenticated customer can supply https://evil.com and receive a valid Stripe portal session that returns to the attacker-controlled host. Reproduction: create a test account, perform a valid checkout to obtain stripe_customer_id, then POST /api/billing/portal with {"origin_url":"https://evil.com"}; observed HTTP 200 with portal_url instead of HTTP 400.
